Joined only when that workbook's trading grid is identical to the primary source's; a differing grid is recorded in benchmarks.json 'skipped' and the series left out rather than realigned.
benchmarkSource.note: SPY and SMH are carried as extra ticker-like columns in the semi and hw_networking workbooks; the SP500 and software workbooks have neither. Extract ONCE from the semi workbook, before any tab build, and join into every universe. This is safe because all four price workbooks share a byte-identical 1,255-day trading grid after drop_calendar_days - verified, not assumed. Extracting per-tab would invite four subtly different date grids.

market_internals.label: Market Internals

excludeTickers.reason: Dominion Energy. Column holds a constant 15 for all 1,255 sessions (distinct value count = 1) while the stock trades near $50-60. This is not a price series - the export carries some other metric under this header.
Cencora. Column runs 0.024 down to 0.0018 across the window while the stock trades near $250-300, and terminal volume collapses to ~64 shares/day. Wrong metric, not a stale price.

Chevron. In the 20260927 export the column holds a constant 27.375 for all 1,255 sessions (distinct value count = 1), with volume pinned at 416,100, while the stock trades near $150-200 - the 20260907 export carried a normal series (97.06 -> 208.60). A broken export column, not a price: re-check on the next vintage and drop this exclusion once it prints a real series again.

market_internals.excludeNote: BNY (Bank of New York Mellon) was excluded through the 20260907 vintage as a wrong-metric column (15.36 -> 10.2); the 20260927 export carries a real price series (52.63 -> 150.15, 1,124 distinct values, normal volume), so the exclusion was removed on that refresh. Positively identified as wrong-metric columns by magnitude against the mapped company names, not merely suspected. The playbook's documented remedy is to exclude at load time with a written reason rather than let them flow into breadth and the composite. Re-check on every refresh - a corrected file can relocate bad data instead of fixing it.
market_internals.shardZNote: 495 shards; only the default z-window ships. The focused tabs carry all four because their universes are 34-120 names.

pharma.label: Pharma Stock Dynamics

source.stem: US pharma stocks 5y price and volume

excludeTickers.reason: Sub-penny OTC quote, not a tradeable pharma price series. Falls from 1.39 to a 0.0001 low (0.005 at the last print), carries 73 zero-volume days, and posts 44 single-day moves beyond +200%/-80% - up to +11,900% on a one-tick change. The composite chains the cross-sectional mean of DAILY returns, so a single such day would add ~240 points to a 49-name index. Excluded at load time.

pharma.history: Added on the 20260927 vintage, the first delivery of this workbook. XLV, IHE and XHE ride as extra columns and are used as benchmarks, not members. The equal-weight composite is dominated by small specialty and clinical-stage names, while XLV is cap-weighted toward a few large names - expect the two to diverge.

_addingAUniverse: One entry here + config/parameters.json subBaskets entry + scripts/build_<name>.py (a ~12-line copy) + site/tabs/<tab>.html (a ~20-line copy) + one nav link. Nothing in loaders.py, validators.py, indicators.py, interpretation.py, pipeline.py or charts.js changes.
